What’s buzzing on Gen Z’s feed today? Smriti Mandhana takes over as India’s women’s cricket captain, Lionel Messi retires from international football & more

Shambhavi Dixit | Oct 07, 2026, 11:26 IST
Share

From Smriti Mandhana taking over from Harmanpreet Kaur as India’s women’s cricket captain to Lionel Messi retiring from international football, here’s a quick look at what’s making waves today.

The internet never really takes a day off, and neither do our news notifications. From Smriti Mandhana becoming the new captain of India’s women’s cricket team to Novak Djokovic winning the China Open, social media is buzzing with updates. Meanwhile, former India captain Sourav Ganguly has been appointed head coach of Delhi Capitals for the next IPL season, India has recalled Bhuvneshwar Kumar for the New Zealand tour after nearly four years, and Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the new IAF Chief.


From viral moments and celebrity updates to sports, politics and stories making headlines across India and around the world, here’s your quick roundup of everything everyone’s talking about today. Whether it’s a story dominating X, a video going viral on Instagram or a celebrity update taking over your feed, these are the headlines you need to know.

1. Smriti Mandhana takes over from Harmanpreet Kaur as India’s women’s cricket captain

On Tuesday, October 6, senior opener Smriti Mandhana was appointed captain of India’s women’s cricket team after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from the role.

Harmanpreet Kaur announced her decision to step down in a social media post following a review meeting with Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia, women’s cricket team head coach Amol Muzumdar and Mandhana in Guwahati on Monday, October 5.

The star opener now steps into one of the biggest leadership roles in Indian women’s cricket, marking the beginning of a new chapter for the team.

2. Djokovic wins China Open, extends unbeaten record as de Minaur retires injured

Image credit : djokernole | Djokovic wins China Open, extends unbeaten record as de Minaur retires injured
Novak Djokovic won the China Open for the seventh time on Tuesday, October 6, after Alex de Minaur retired at the beginning of the second set of their final in Beijing.

Djokovic won the opening set 7-6 before both players took medical timeouts. De Minaur left the court at the beginning of the second set for treatment on his groin and retired after winning the opening game.

The victory gave Djokovic his 102nd tour-level title, moving him within one title of Roger Federer’s tally of 103 for the second-most titles in the Open Era.

3. Former India captain Sourav Ganguly appointed head coach of Delhi Capitals for the next IPL season

Former India captain Sourav Ganguly is returning as the new head coach of Delhi Capitals for the 2027 IPL season. The appointment marks his first stint as an IPL head coach and sees him replace Hemang Badani at the franchise.

Ganguly has had a long association with the Capitals, dating back to 2019 when he joined the franchise as an advisor. He later served as Director of Cricket for both the men’s and women’s teams, making his latest appointment a continuation of his relationship with the franchise.

The move comes as Delhi Capitals look to build a stronger campaign after finishing sixth in IPL 2026 and continuing their wait for a maiden IPL title. Ganguly, known for his aggressive leadership style and experience in building competitive teams, will now be tasked with shaping the squad ahead of the 2027 season.


4. India recalls Bhuvneshwar Kumar for the New Zealand tour after four years

Veteran Indian pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar is set to return to the national team after nearly four years. The 36-year-old has been included in India’s T20I squad for the upcoming tour of New Zealand, marking a surprise comeback for one of the country’s most experienced white-ball bowlers.

Bhuvneshwar’s last appearance for India came against New Zealand in November 2022. His recall follows a strong IPL 2026 campaign, where he picked up 28 wickets and finished just one wicket behind Kagiso Rabada in the race for the Purple Cap.

Known particularly for his ability to swing the ball and make an impact with the new ball, Bhuvneshwar’s experience could add depth to India’s T20I bowling attack. His return also comes with an eye on the 2027 ODI World Cup, although questions remain over whether his body can handle the demands of longer white-ball campaigns.

5. Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit appointed new IAF Chief

Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, becoming the next chief of the Indian Air Force. He will take charge in the rank of Air Chief Marshal from the afternoon of October 31, 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, who is set to retire on the same day.

Dixit is currently serving as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff, a position he assumed in July 2026. He was commissioned into the fighter stream of the IAF in December 1986 and has accumulated more than 3,500 hours of flying experience.


During his nearly four-decade career, he has flown several aircraft, including the Mirage 2000, Jaguar, Tejas, MiG variants, IL-78 and Hawk. He has also been involved in major operations and exercises, including Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak, Cope India and Operation Sindoor.

6. Lionel Messi retires from international football as Argentina defeats Benin

Image credit : Lionel Messi | Lionel Messi retires from international football as Argentina defeats Benin
Lionel Messi has officially retired from his extraordinary 21-year international career with Argentina. The football icon made his final appearance for the national team in a farewell match against Benin at Buenos Aires’ Estadio Monumental, where Argentina secured a 3-0 victory.

And, fittingly, Messi signed off in style. The 39-year-old scored one goal and assisted two others as Argentina dominated Benin in front of more than 85,000 emotional fans. The match was more than a friendly; it became a celebration of one of football's greatest careers.

Messi leaves Argentina as the country’s most-capped player, with 208 appearances and 126 goals. His international legacy includes two Copa América titles and the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the trophy that finally ended Argentina’s long wait for football’s biggest prize.

Although his Argentina chapter is now over, Messi is expected to continue his club career with Inter Miami. His farewell marks the end of an era for Argentina and for a generation of fans who watched him become one of the greatest players in football history.


So, from Smriti Mandhana taking over as India’s women’s cricket captain and Sourav Ganguly returning as head coach of Delhi Capitals for the next IPL season to Lionel Messi officially retiring from international football, these are some of the stories currently making waves across the internet.
